title: What Hotels Get Wrong About Direct Bookings in 2026
summary: The 2019 playbook never reached the three points guests fail. Only 54.2% of DACH hotels can finish a booking on their own site. Direct booking is infrastructure, not marketing.
body_markdown:
Common questions


## FAQ


### What do hotels get wrong about direct bookings in 2026?


They treat a missing path as a marketing problem. The usual advice is still a better website, a best-rate guarantee, and a loyalty offer. Guests already try to book direct. They fail when the hotel's own site cannot complete a reservation, when the phone that is meant to finish it does not answer, and when a new answer engine books the channel that can.


In an enrichment of 26,707 hotels in Germany, Austria and Switzerland with live websites (June 2026), only 54.2% run a real direct-booking engine. That is missing infrastructure, not a weak campaign.


### Why has the usual direct-booking playbook stalled?


Because it improves the look of the hotel and the offer around the last step, and leaves the last step unchanged. HOTREC's European Hotel Distribution Study 2026, covering bookings in 2025, finds that direct's share of European hotel bookings fell by six percentage points from 2013, to 51.3%, while online travel agencies rose from 19.7% to 29.9%.


In Germany, realtime booking on the hotel's own website is 13.9% of overnights, up from 6.1% in 2013. The phone is still 18.1%. Twelve years of website work more than doubled the live site share and still left it smaller than the phone.


### How many hotels can actually be booked on their own website?


In that same 26,707-hotel DACH enrichment, only 54.2% run a real direct-booking engine, which means nearly half cannot complete a reservation on their own site. Detection is a floor: it depends on what the hotel publishes, and a non-standard engine can be missed. At least 13.3% of the same hotels confirm bookings by manual callback.


The fuller split, including hotels with no online path at all, is in the[website argument](https://www.codyco.ai/blog/why-guests-still-call-when-everything-is-on-the-website) .


### What happens when a guest cannot finish a direct booking?


The request does not queue. The guest tries the number on the page, and[that line is already missed at scale](https://www.codyco.ai/blog/the-state-of-hotel-missed-calls) . If the phone does not answer, the next open door is usually an agency listing, or another hotel. The hotel then pays commission on a guest who had already chosen it, or loses the stay. Almost none of this appears in a review.


[A reachability complaint is rare](https://www.codyco.ai/blog/what-one-hotel-review-tells-you-about-missed-calls) because the guest has already solved the problem another way.


### Is AI search a new hotel booking channel?


It is becoming one, and it books the path that already finishes. In August 2026 Google began rolling out hotel booking inside AI Mode in the United States, through a partner list of online travel agencies and large hotel groups. The launch is not a European product.


The structural point still holds: an answer engine asked to complete a booking will use inventory that already closes. A hotel whose own site cannot take a reservation is a name in the answer, not a bookable path. That is not a measured claim that answer engines cannot find a given hotel.


### How can a hotel test whether it can finish a direct booking?


Test the last step, not the look of the page. Try to book tonight on the hotel's own site and see whether the next step is a completed reservation or a form, a callback promise, or a phone number. Call the published number after hours and during a busy check-in.


Ask an answer engine to book that hotel for those dates and see whether the completed path is the hotel's site or an agency listing. If the hotel runs several properties, run the same three checks on each one. A campaign cannot close a door the hotel never built.
